newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says Germany may fail EMU needs in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Buba says Germany may fail EMU needs in 1996.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday that it could not rule out Germany in 1996 exceeding debt and deficit level requirements in the Maastricht Treaty needed for membership the single European currency.

"From today's vantage point, it cannot be ruled out that the budget deficit may reach up to four percent of the gross domestic product in the current year after totalling 3.5 percent of GDP last year," the Bundesbank said in its September report.
The Maastricht Treaty calls for, among other factors, nations interested in joining the planned currency union to have budget deficits of not more than three percent of GDP.
The report also said the Bundesbank believed the government's budget could rise "somewhat" above 60 percent of the country's GDP, as outlined in the treaty.
Initial membership in the new currency, slated to begin in January 1999, is scheduled to be decided in early 1998.
